title: parameterized-runbook-templates-and-cli-instantiator
author: Ravi Patel
description:
Motivation: On-call responders often need a concise, environment-aware runbook that pulls only the relevant steps and injects safe defaults (service names, canary thresholds, playbook parameters). We currently ship monolithic runbooks which lead to duplication and slower oncall response. This PR introduces a small templating layer for runbooks plus a CLI that instantiates a parameterized runbook for the active incident context and validates it against a lightweight schema.

What this changes: Adds a runbook template format (YAML-based) with parameter declarations, defaults and validation hints; a runbook-instantiator CLI (incident-bot runbook render) that fetches incident context (service, region, severity, active alerts) and outputs a sanitized runbook JSON or formatted markdown; a server-side validation hook used by incident-bot when attaching runbooks to incidents; and updated docs and tests. The templates are intentionally opinionated and small to avoid lock-in.

Key features: 1) Parameter declarations with types (string, int, percentage, enum, bool) and safe defaults. 2) Conditional sections: steps can declare conditions (e.g., if kvcache_enabled == true). 3) Safe substitution: CLI performs escaping and disallows secrets in output; placeholders marked secrets will be redacted unless running with a vault token. 4) Lint/validate command: incident-bot runbook validate <file> with helpful diagnostics. 5) Regression/backfill tool to convert a subset of existing canonical runbooks into templates (opt-in).

Backward compatibility: Existing monolithic runbooks still work; the server accepts both template and instantiated runbook payloads. When a template is attached to an incident, the platform stores the rendered snapshot to preserve the historical record.

Usage examples: 
- Render quick CLI for oncall: `incident-bot runbook render --incident 2026-02-10-INC1234 --format markdown > oncall.md`
- Validate before upload: `incident-bot runbook validate mydb-failover.template.yaml`

Testing: Unit tests for template parsing, type coercion and conditional expansion included. Integration tests simulate incident context with mocked alert payloads and verify output snapshot is deterministic and contains no redacted secrets unless vault token provided. CI runs lint, unit, integration, and e2e smoke (the e2e smoke uses a small fixture incident).

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind `runbook_templates` flag. Default off for orgs created before 2025-10-01 to avoid surprising changes. Gradual rollout: enable in staging, then 10% of orgs, monitor runbook-render latency and size, then 100%.

Security note: We intentionally do not inject Kubernetes or cloud provider credentials. Templates may reference a `{{vault://path#key}}` marker that remains unresolved unless the operator passes a short-lived vault token to the CLI. Server-side rendering uses the same guardrails.

Related: ENG-1972 (oncall ergonomics), ENG-2038 (runbook storage compaction).
commit_summary: 2 main commits: (1) runbook template schema, parser, and validator; (2) CLI + server integration + docs + tests. Small follow-ups for lint fixes and test flakiness fixes.
review_comments: Samantha Lee: Nice separation of concerns. A few nits on validator error messages and a suggestion to return structured validation errors for the UI.
Ravi Patel (author): Addressed nits, switched validator to return a list of structured issues (code, path, message). Added more tests for enum coercion.
Diego Moralez: Can we gate the CLI so it fails-fast if a vault token is supplied but missing expected capability? Added a check in pkg/security/redaction.go; please confirm.
Priya Kapoor: Integration tests look flakey on Windows runners (path separators). Convert glob to filepath.Join in the test harness. Fixed.

QA (Lina Zhou): Verified rendered markdown for three incident scenarios and sanity-checked for secrets redaction. Found a missing default for db_failover_timeout; author added default and updated fixtures.
SRE oncall (approver): Approved after seeing the staging rollout metrics — render latency < 120ms P99 and snapshot size acceptable.
release_notes: Adds parameterized runbook templates and a CLI to render and validate them. Feature gated; opt-in conversion tool for legacy runbooks. See docs/runbooks/templating.md for usage and migration guidance.
migration_instructions: For operators: to migrate a runbook, run `scripts/convert_legacy_runbooks.py --input legacy.yaml --output template.yaml` and validate the result. Enable feature flag in org settings to allow template attachments. Backups: existing instantiated runbooks remain immutable in incident history.
performance_considerations: Render is CPU-light; added telemetry (pkg/telemetry/runbook_metrics.go) to track render latency and template expansion size. Observed median render under 20ms in CI fixtures; P99 under 120ms in staging during canary.
qa_notes: QA smoke checklist: validate CLI output for severity=sev1/2 combinations, ensure secrets are redacted, validate schema error messages, run conversion on three representative runbooks and inspect diffs.
notes_for_release_manager: Feature gated. Coordinate staged flag rollout with platform; add an announcement to the oncall runbook docs and include a brief demo in next oncall rotation meeting.
